answer: One daily vote requires a sparrow-monitoring AI agent to reserve an exclusive certified sensor. A beacon selects auditors to test its non-exportable cipher key with a fresh encrypted nonce and sign agent/day/device receipts. Validators deny votes for failed checks or duplicate device IDs that day. n voting keys need n sensors; parallelism cannot reuse IDs. Sensors are reusable capital, not a daily fee. This assumes one certificate per device and unclonable keys; colluding auditors can fake receipts, and wealthy operators can buy more sensors.
